chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
title: Card games, pool and the radio parlor at San Jacinto
summary: San Jacinto offered cards, pool tables and a parlor with a radio for members.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I think at Santa, Santa used to be a place for nice, clean pleasure, you know. Yeah. The fellas would go play cards there and, you know, and just play poker, cards and all that. They had a couple of pool tables. Yeah.
Did they have regular gaming rooms where you played cards? Yeah.
They had everything you could mention. Any kind.

And then you had the parlor. In the parlor they had the radio. Go sit down and listen to the radio. They'd go sit down. Some fellas didn't like to gamble. They'd go sit down and enjoy that. A whole lot of the members would enjoy that and them would didn't gamble or nothing, you know.
